_comment: Copy to config.json and adjust. config.json is gitignored because it
carries LAN addresses. Secrets are never in here -- only the NAME of the
environment variable that holds each one, which lives in .env.
Anything omitted falls back to DEFAULTS in collector.py, so a deployed
box only needs to carry what it actually overrides. That is why adding a
new setting never requires touching the Pi.

_commits_comment: Repos are discovered, not listed. `discover` is on by default; the
keys below are shown at their defaults so they are easy to find.
`repos` overrides discovery entirely when it is non-empty -- keep it
empty unless you want this panel pinned to specific repos, because a
hand-written list is exactly what goes stale without telling you.
`untracked` is unrelated to either: those are local projects with no
git remote, which GitHub cannot see however hard it looks.

_healthchecks_comment: A once-a-day pass, kept as a ninety-day history in
state_dir/healthchecks.json. There is no hour-of-day setting on
purpose: the checks run the first time a poll notices that today has
no entry yet, so `interval_s` is only how quickly the date rollover
gets noticed -- not how often the checks run.
A check whose instrument is missing is left out of the day rather
than counted as a failure, so this runs clean on a dev Mac with the
Pi-only rows (throttling, soc temp, memory) simply absent.
The zero_* keys are the only Zero W touchpoint here and stay flat:
the config merge is one level deep, so a nested block would be
replaced wholesale by a box that overrode a single key.

_cmo_comment: The Daily CMO job's own files, read off local disk -- nothing here
goes over the network. base_dir is the working directory the job
runs in; the source reads heartbeat/cmo.json (required),
The source is dormant, not failing, until the job has run once and
written a heartbeat. That is a statement about the box, not an
error, and it needs no configuration to say so.
history_days and briefings_max are display windows, not retention:
this never deletes anything the job wrote.
Flat keys, like healthchecks' zero_* ones and for the same reason:
the config merge is one level deep, so a nested block would be
replaced wholesale by a box that overrode a single key inside it.

_mail_comment: The Gmail mirror under base_dir/mail, read off local disk. The
collector never talks to Gmail and holds no mail credentials: the
app password lives with the poller and the actions worker, which are
timer- and path-driven scripts with no listening socket between them;
this program reads the files they write and queues spool entries for
So there is no token_env here and nothing to add to .env. The source
is dormant, not failing, until the poller's first run writes
mail/state.json -- a statement about the box rather than an error.
list_max is a display window like briefings_max: nothing is deleted,
and anything the list leaves out is still on the message route.
poll_stale_after_s is the mailbox's own staleness, not our copy's --
the poller fires every 5 minutes, so 1200 is four missed fires.
Its own base_dir even though it is the same directory the cmo block uses:
the config merge is one level deep, so a box that moved one of the two
would otherwise have to move both. Flat keys for the same reason.

_chat_comment: The chat assistant's conversations, under base_dir/threads. This is
the one block here that is NOT a source: it has no interval_s and no
stale_after_s, nothing polls it, and it never joins /v1/telemetry.
A conversation is interactive -- the CHAT tab asks for the thread it
is looking at, on its own cadence -- and a chat that also arrived once
a minute inside a document about disk temperature would be a second
copy of the same state going stale on its own schedule.
The collector writes the thread record, the user turn, the .queue
spool entry and the .stop flag, and nothing else. chat-runner.py,
started by halftone-chat.path when .queue stops being empty, writes
the status, the streaming partial, the assistant turn and the claude
session id, and deletes both flags. One writer per field.
This process starts no model and holds no credentials for one. The
runner is where claude is invoked, under its own unit, with its own
working directory and its own permission allowlist (env/.claude/).
ReadWritePaths=/home/pi/halftone-chat in its unit, for the reason
every other write path here needs one: ProtectHome is read-only, so
without it every send fails EROFS while every read carries on working.

_tts_comment: The Kokoro voice service on the Mac, an external TTS host reached
over the tailnet on port 8790. The collector only proxies:
the browser never talks to the Mac, which is what keeps the audio
same-origin with the page that plays it. Like chat, this is not a
source -- nothing polls it and it never joins /v1/telemetry.
The shared secret is not here, per the rule at the top of this
file: it lives in .env as HALFTONE_TTS_KEY and is forwarded to the
This block has no entry in DEFAULTS, and that absence is the off
switch: leave it out of config.json and voice is simply disabled --
